summary: Approximate the unknown matrix $A$ within the public linear subspace $\mathcal{L}=\operatorname{span}\{B_1,\ldots,B_q\}$.

metric.description_zh: Define $\operatorname{OPT}=\min_{B\in\mathcal L}\|A-B\|_{\mathrm F}$; success requires $\|A-\widehat B\|_{\mathrm F}\le\gamma\operatorname{OPT}+\alpha\|A\|_{\mathrm F}$. The finite-dimensional linear space is closed, so a minimizer exists. If $A=0$, output zero.

metric.finiteness_conditions: The matrix is finite-dimensional and satisfies the model's spectral, norm, and function assumptions. Zero denominators and zero optimal error follow the conventions explicitly stated here.

algorithms.description_zh: Algorithms may use private randomness and choose query vectors adaptively from the declared domain using all previous responses. norms.definition: Euclidean vector norm $\|z\|_2=(\sum_i|z_i|^2)^{1/2}$ and matrix operator norm $\|M\|_{\rm op}=\max_{\|z\|_2=1}\|Mz\|_2$; define $\|M\|_F=(\sum_{ij}|M_{ij}|^2)^{1/2}$.

comparators.definition: Approximate the unknown matrix $A$ within the public linear subspace $\mathcal L=\operatorname{span}\{B_1,\ldots,B_q\}$. Define $\operatorname{OPT}=\min_{B\in\mathcal L}\|A-B\|_{\mathrm F}$; success requires $\|A-\widehat B\|_{\mathrm F}\le\gamma\operatorname{OPT}+\alpha\|A\|_{\mathrm F}$. Finite-dimensional linear subspaces are closed, so the minimum exists. If $A=0$, the output must be zero.

proofs.title: Deterministic basis reconstruction followed by projection onto the public linear matrix space.
proofs.body: Recover all $d$ columns by standard basis queries. Frobenius orthogonal projection onto the public linear span is a finite-dimensional least-squares problem in known coefficients and is uncharged. Its output attains the exact optimum residual, including zero optimum.
proofs.scope: All model, oracle, algorithm, guarantee, quantity, resource-projection, and region conditions attached to the mapped bounds remain in force.

evidence.supports: Definition 7 of QSL defines the q-dimensional linear matrix family. Corollary 3 and the covering argument in Theorem 6 give $(3+\eta)\operatorname{OPT}+\alpha\|A\|_F$, with $\eta=\gamma-3$. Both multiplication directions are allowed; public-basis and covering-net computations are uncharged.
